chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar Al-Yamani, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'They claim that the citron eaten on an empty stomach is the best of what it can be.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said, 'If it is before the meal, it is good, and if it is after the meal, it is good, and better, and best.'

key_terms.أَجْوَدُ: The best, most excellent, or highest quality.
key_terms.الْأُتْرُجَّ: Citron or citron fruit, a type of citrus known for its medicinal and culinary uses.
key_terms.عَلَى الرِّيقِ: On an empty stomach; literally 'upon the saliva', indicating no food is present in the stomach.

ai.seo_question: Is it better to eat citron before or after a meal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses a contemporary medical opinion regarding the optimal timing for consuming citron (utrujj). He validates the view that while citron is beneficial on an empty stomach, its therapeutic and gustatory qualities are enhanced when consumed after a meal, reflecting the Shia tradition of integrating practical health advice with spiritual guidance. This clarification underscores the Imam’s role in refining communal understanding of dietary laws and wellness.
